title: Send Analytics and find a playback session
lead: Play with Analytics enabled, then find the collected session in Bitmovin Dashboard. Use the Web app’s local QoE values and logs to inspect the current playback.

rows: Player Lab Web or native app
Apply settings and inspect playback state and applied code.
Send supported events and playback context to the selected Analytics license.
Find the session using the same license, period and filters.

blocks.text: Find a playback in the Dashboard

items: Play a video in an app configured for Analytics. Note the settings, source, device and playback time. On the public Pages app, also read the collection notice.
Sign in to Bitmovin Dashboard, open Observability and select the collector’s Analytics license.
Choose a period containing the playback and check the time zone. Filter by content or browser, then find the playback through Plays or Latest Sessions under Audience.
Match the session time with the app’s event log. Continue to the Dashboard chapter for browser quality comparisons or error investigation.

blocks.caption: Official Bitmovin demo screen showing the license, period, Global Filters and Video Title selectors. Values are dummy data. This older screen uses an Analytics menu label and layout that may differ from the current Dashboard. Source: the official sandbox article linked below. © Bitmovin.

blocks.text: You need access to the selected Analytics license. Playing the public demo does not grant access to its destination account. Configure your own license in a local app to inspect your data. A collection notice or browser-local value alone does not confirm backend receipt.

items.label: Compare quality and investigate errors in the Dashboard

items: Play VOD HLS or another finite source in the Web app. Read Player state and Playback quality below the player.
Seek and compare Seek/Seeked in the log with seek time. Live playback uses TimeShift/TimeShifted.
Pause and resume. Manual pauses do not count as rebuffering; StallStarted/StallEnded after playback begins increases the interruption count.
For configuration comparisons, copy Show applied configuration code. Draft edits are excluded. Reload the source to start a new measurement.

blocks.text: QoE means Quality of Experience. These values come from the current Player’s events; their population and definitions differ from Dashboard Analytics.

rows: SourceLoaded to the first Playing event. Waiting before a manual Play can contribute; this is not the Analytics VIDEO_STARTUPTIME definition.
Stall time / (playing time + stall time) after startup. Manual pauses and initial buffering are excluded.
Number of Error events received by the current session, rather than the number of affected viewers.
Latest Seek or TimeShift request to its completion event.
Device wall clock minus the playback wall-clock timestamp; requires usable source timing such as HLS Program Date Time (PDT).
The SDK lowlatency.getLatency() value: distance from the live edge, rather than from real time.

blocks.text: A dash or needs PDT is not zero latency. QoE latency fields can retain their last valid value if timing becomes unavailable, so also check Player state for the current source.
Use events to explain a change

The log shows events such as SourceLoaded, Play, Playing, Paused, Seek, TimeShift, StallStarted and Error with local timestamps. It retains up to 80 lines, newest first. TimeChanged updates readouts but is omitted from the log.
Loading or unloading a source, or destroying the Player, resets measurements. Theme or UI changes retain them; playback end stops the totals. Reload before comparing another trial.

The public Pages app sends Analytics when configured. It hides aggregate queries because Pages has no server to hold an account API key. Use the chapters below for aggregate definitions and API queries.
